subject: maths
title: Angles on a Straight Line and at a Point
seo_title: Year 6 Angles on a Straight Line and at a Point Worksheets: Vertically Opposite and Unknown Angles (Free, with Answers)
short_title: Angles on a line and at a point
standard_text: Identify the relationships between angles on a straight line, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles; use these to determine unknown angles, communicating reasoning
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets for the Australian Curriculum: angles on a straight line (180°), angles at a point (360°) and vertically opposite angles, finding unknown angles in diagrams and explaining the reasoning, with clock, pizza and roof truss problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, angles at a point add up to 360°, and vertically opposite angles are equal.
key_sub: Add the angles you know, then subtract from 180° or 360°. Do not trust how an angle looks: use a fact and show each step.
body_html:
Three angle facts

To find an unknown angle, look for the fact that fits the picture. Add the angles you know, then subtract from the total.

Where the angles areAngle fact
On a straight lineThey add up to 180° (a straight angle)
At a point (all the way round)They add up to 360° (a revolution)
Vertically opposite (two straight lines cross)They are equal
Next to each other where two lines crossThey add up to 180°

Worked examples

Straight line

Three angles on a straight line are 48°, 70° and ?. Find ?.

Straight line, so the total is 180°. 48° + 70° = 118°. 180° − 118° = 62°. Check: 48° + 70° + 62° = 180°.

Answer: 62°

At a point

Angles at a point are 200°, 95° and ?. Find ?.

At a point, so the total is 360°. 200° + 95° = 295°. 360° − 295° = 65°.

Answer: 65°

Explain your reasoning

Three straight lines meet at a point (picture above). Find ?.

Step 1: 40°, 65° and the angle between them are on a straight line, so that angle is 180° − 105° = 75°. Step 2: ? is vertically opposite that angle, and vertically opposite angles are equal.

Answer: 75°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 360° for a straight line, or 180° at a pointStraight line: 180°. All the way round: 360°
Adding the known angles and giving that total as the answerAdd the known angles, then subtract the total from 180° or 360°
Thinking two angles are equal because they look the sameOnly use a fact: vertically opposite, or marked as equal. Then calculate
Thinking vertically opposite angles add up to 180°Opposite angles are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°

faq.q: What do Year 6 students learn about angles in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: They learn that angles on a straight line add up to 180°, angles at a point add up to 360° and vertically opposite angles are equal, and they use these facts to find unknown angles and explain their reasoning.

faq.q: How do you find a missing angle on a straight line?
faq.a: Add the angles you know and subtract the total from 180°. For example, if the other angles are 48° and 70°, the missing angle is 180° − 118° = 62°.
When two straight lines cross they make four angles. The angles opposite each other are vertically opposite and always equal; the angles next to each other add up to 180°.

faq.q: Should students measure missing angles with a protractor?
faq.a: No, they should calculate them with the angle facts and show each step. Angles that look equal may not be, and diagrams in tests are often not drawn to scale.

items.e: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 73° = 107°.

items.q: A straight line is split into three angles. Two of them are 65° and 47°. What is the third angle?
items.e: 65° + 47° = 112°. 180° − 112° = 68°. (112° is the two angles added, not the missing one.)

items.q: Two angles on a straight line. One is an acute angle of 38°. What is the other angle?
items.e: 180° − 38° = 142°. It is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse. (52° is 90° − 38°, which is for a right angle.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: 25° + 95° = 120°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so 180° − 120° = 60°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. What is the value of x?
Three equal angles together make a straight line. How big is each angle?
items.e: The three angles add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°. (120° would come from using 360°.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: First add the angles you know: 48° + 70° = 118°. Then subtract from 180°: 180° − 118° = 62°.

items.q: Isla says a = 50°, because it looks the same size as the 50° angle. Is she right?
items.e: Do not trust how an angle looks: work it out. 50° + 76° = 126°, and 180° − 126° = 54°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.q: The whole angle is a right angle. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: A right angle is 90°. 90° − 62° = 28°. (180° − 62° = 118° would be for a straight line.)

items.q: The two angles marked a are equal. What is a?
items.e: 180° − 70° = 110°. The two equal angles share it: 110° ÷ 2 = 55°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The small square is a right angle: 90°. 90° + 35° = 125°, and 180° − 125° = 55°.
The angles are on a straight line, so they add up to 180°, not 360°. 180° − 130° = 50°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 115° = 65°. (360° − 115° = 245° would be for angles at a point.)

items.q: Two angles on a straight line. One angle is 4 times as big as the other. How big is the smaller angle?
items.e: The angles are 1 part and 4 parts: 5 parts = 180°. 1 part = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°. (The larger angle is 4 × 36° = 144°.)
The line is tilted, but it is still straight: 180° − 48° = 132°.

items.q: Angles on a straight line add up to …
items.e: A straight angle is a half turn: 180°. Two right angles make a straight line.

items.q: Two angles are next to each other. One is 125° and the other is 65°. Can they make a straight line?
items.e: 125° + 65° = 190°. Angles on a straight line must add up to exactly 180°, so they cannot.

items.q: Two angles sit on a straight line. One of them is 74°. How big is the other angle?

items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (180° ÷ 3 = 60° would be a straight line.)

items.q: Angles at a point add up to …
items.e: Angles at a point make a full turn (a revolution): 360°.

items.q: A reflex angle of 250° and one other angle make a full turn. How big is the other angle?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. 360° − 250° = 110°. (70° comes from 250° − 180°, and 610° from adding.)
Add the angles you know, then subtract from 360°: 360° − 250° = 110°. 250° is the total of the two angles, not the missing angle.

items.q: Four angles are at a point. Three of them are 95°, 120° and 85°. What is the fourth angle?

items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° − 130° = 230°. (50° comes from using 180°, and 490° from adding.)
360° − 100° = 260°. The two equal angles share it: 260° ÷ 2 = 130°.

items.q: Three angles at a point are x, 2x and 3x. What is x?
Three angles are at a point. Two of them are 140° each. What is the third angle?
items.e: 140° + 140° = 280°. 360° − 280° = 80°. (220° comes from subtracting only one 140°.)

items.q: Can angles of 150°, 120° and 100° fit around a point with no gaps or overlaps?
items.e: 150° + 120° + 100° = 370°. Angles at a point must add up to exactly 360°, so they would overlap by 10°.

items.q: How many angles of 45° fit exactly around a point?
items.e: 360° ÷ 45° = 8. (4 is how many fit on a straight line: 180° ÷ 45° = 4.)
Angles at a point add up to 360°. 110° + 135° = 245°, and 360° − 245° = 115°.

items.q: Two angles are at a point. One is 5 times as big as the other. How big is the larger angle?
items.e: 1 part + 5 parts = 6 parts = 360°. 1 part = 60°, so the larger angle is 5 × 60° = 300° (a reflex angle). (150° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Four angles are at a point. One is a right angle and the other three are equal. How big is each of the three equal angles?
items.e: 360° − 90° = 270°. The three equal angles share it: 270° ÷ 3 = 90°.
The small square is 90°. 90° + 125° + 60° = 275°, and 360° − 275° = 85°. (175° comes from forgetting the right angle.)

items.q: Five equal angles fit exactly around a point. How big is each angle?
Two straight lines cross. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 65° angle, so they are equal: 65°.
p and 105° are on a straight line: 180° − 105° = 75°. q is vertically opposite 105°, so 105°. r is vertically opposite p: 75°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 72° angle, so they are equal: 72°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What is the value of y?
items.e: 2y is vertically opposite 80°, so 2y = 80°. Then y = 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
The missing angle is vertically opposite the 155° angle, so they are equal: 155°.
The missing angle is vertically opposite the 145° angle, so they are equal: 145°.
The missing angle and 58° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 58° = 122°.
The missing angle and 146° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 146° = 34°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What do all four angles add up to?
items.e: The four angles go all the way around the crossing point, so they add up to 360°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 80° angle, so it is also 80°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 40° angle, so they are equal: 40°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One angle is 27°. How big is the angle vertically opposite it?
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is also 27°. (153° is the angle next to it.)
The missing angle and 130° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 130° = 50°.

items.q: Leo says that vertically opposite angles add up to 180°. Is he right?
c: Yes, they are on a straight line
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal. It is the angles next to each other (on a straight line) that add up to 180°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Two vertically opposite angles add up to 100°. How big is each of the other two angles?
items.e: The two equal opposite angles are 100° ÷ 2 = 50° each. The angles next to them are 180° − 50° = 130°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles is a right angle. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The angle next to 90° is 180° − 90° = 90°, and the opposite angles are equal. So all four angles are 90°.
Vertically opposite angles are across the crossing point from each other: a and c (also b and d). Angles next to each other, like a and b, add up to 180°.
a is next to 86° on a straight line, not opposite it. 180° − 86° = 94°. Angles can look equal and still be different, so use the angle facts.
The missing angle and 75° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 75° = 105°.
a is on a straight line with 64°: 180° − 64° = 116°. b is vertically opposite 64°, so it is 64°. c is vertically opposite a, so it is 116°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The three angles above the flat line are on a straight line. 40° + 75° = 115°, and 180° − 115° = 65°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The angle between 55° and ? is vertically opposite 65°, so it is 65°. Then on the straight line: 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross at right angles. One more line starts at the crossing point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The lines cross at right angles, so all four angles they make are 90°. The angle between the downward line and the right-hand line is 90°, so ? = 90° − 50° = 40°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Which angle is vertically opposite angle b?
items.e: Follow the two lines that make angle b through the crossing point. The angle between them on the other side is e.

items.q: Two straight lines cross, and one more line starts at the crossing point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: Step 1: next to 65° on the straight line is 180° − 65° = 115°. Step 2: the angle below, between the sloping line and the flat line, is vertically opposite it, so it is 115°. Step 3: 115° − 70° = 45°.
a is on a straight line with 128°: 180° − 128° = 52°. b is vertically opposite 128°, so b = 128°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.

items.e: The 70° angle and ? are on the straight line below it: 180° − 70° = 110°. The 50° angle does not help here.

items.q: Three straight lines cross at one point and make six equal angles. What is x?
items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. (30° comes from 180° ÷ 6.)

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: Step 1: the angle between 40° and 65° on the straight line is 180° − 40° − 65° = 75°. Step 2: the missing angle is vertically opposite it, so it is 75°.

items.q: Oliver says the missing angle is 60°, because all three angles look equal. Is he right?
items.e: 61° + 60° = 121°, and 180° − 121° = 59°. The angles look almost the same, but they are not equal.
2x and 4x are next to each other on a straight line: 6x = 180°, so x = 30°. (60° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What is the value of a?
items.e: The two angles are vertically opposite, so they are equal: 2a = a + 20°. Take a from both sides: a = 20°. Check: 2 × 20° = 40° and 20° + 20° = 40°.
a: 180° − 50° − 60° = 70° (straight line). b is vertically opposite 50°, and c is vertically opposite 60°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross, and one more line starts at the crossing point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The three angles above the flat line are on a straight line. 70° + 55° = 125°, and 180° − 125° = 55°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross, and one more line starts at the crossing point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: Step 1: on the straight line, the angle at the right is 180° − 55° − 55° = 70°. Step 2: the missing angle is vertically opposite it, so it is 70°.

items.q: The minute hand turns for 20 minutes. Through how many degrees does it turn?
items.e: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, so 6° each minute. 20 × 6° = 120°. (240° is the other 40 minutes.)

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of the analog clock at 10 o’clock?
items.e: From 10 to 12 is 2 hour spaces. Each space is 30°, so 2 × 30° = 60°. (300° is the reflex angle the other way round.)

items.q: At the top of a roof truss, the two sloping rafters meet the upright king post. Each rafter makes an angle of 62° with the post. What is the angle between the two rafters?
items.e: The angle between the rafters is made of the two angles next to the post: 62° + 62° = 124°.
The angles at the centre add up to 360°. 100° + 80° + 95° = 275°, and 360° − 275° = 85°.

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 5 o’clock?
items.e: Each hour space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. (210° is the larger angle, the other way round.)

items.q: A pair of scissors is like two straight lines crossing at the screw. The handles are opened to an angle of 35°. What is the angle between the blades?
items.e: The angle between the blades is vertically opposite the angle between the handles, so it is equal: 35°.

items.q: Two straight roads cross. One angle between them is 72°. What do the two obtuse angles add up to?
items.e: Each obtuse angle is 180° − 72° = 108°. The two obtuse angles are vertically opposite, so they are equal: 108° + 108° = 216°.

items.q: At which time do the hands of a clock make a straight angle (180°)?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point to 12 and 6, in a straight line: 6 × 30° = 180°. At 3 and 9 o’clock they make a right angle.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices from the centre. Cooper eats 3 slices. What angle at the centre do the slices that are left make?
items.e: Each slice is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. 5 slices are left: 5 × 45° = 225°. (135° is the 3 slices that were eaten.)

items.q: Charlotte faces east and turns clockwise until she faces north. How many degrees does she turn?
items.e: Clockwise from east: to south is 90°, to west is 180°, to north is 270°. (90° would be turning anticlockwise.)

items.q: At 3 o’clock, what is the reflex angle between the hands of a clock?
items.e: The smaller angle is a right angle, 90°. The reflex angle goes the other way round: 360° − 90° = 270°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Five of the six angles are 40°, 60°, 80°, 40° and 60°. What is the sixth angle?
items.e: All six angles are at a point, so they add up to 360°. 40° + 60° + 80° + 40° + 60° = 280°, and 360° − 280° = 80°. Check: it is vertically opposite the other 80° angle.

items.q: A skateboard ramp starts on flat ground and rises at an angle of 25° to the ground. What is the obtuse angle between the ramp and the ground on the other side of where it starts?
items.e: The two angles are on the straight ground, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 25° = 155°.

items.q: The legs of a folding beach chair cross like an X. The angle between the legs at the top is 50°. What is the angle between the legs at the side of the X?
items.e: The side angle is next to the 50° angle on a straight leg, so 180° − 50° = 130°.

items.q: In a roof truss, a sloping strut meets the straight bottom beam. The angle on one side of the strut is 58°. What is the angle on the other side?
items.e: The two angles are on a straight line (the beam), so they add up to 180°. 180° − 58° = 122°.

items.q: In a roof truss, two struts meet the straight bottom beam at the same point. Above the beam they make three angles: 48°, 75° and one more. What is the third angle?
items.e: The three angles are on the straight beam, so they add up to 180°. 48° + 75° = 123°, and 180° − 123° = 57°.

items.q: A ceiling fan has 5 equal blades spaced evenly around the centre. What is the angle between two blades next to each other?
items.e: The blades share the full turn: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°. (36° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: William cuts a round pizza into 6 equal slices. Every cut goes through the centre. What angle does each slice make at the centre?
items.e: The slices go all the way around the centre: 360°. 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. (30° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Noah faces north and turns clockwise until he faces south-east. How many degrees does he turn?
items.e: North to east is a right angle (90°). East to south-east is half a right angle (45°). 90° + 45° = 135°.

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of the analog clock at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 hour spaces go around 360°, so each is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.
